観.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> hops to the end of a <part>diving board</part> high above the town pool and sets up a tiny <part>camera</part> on its tripod. From up there it can see roofs, parks and the sea beyond. Click! It's the best <kanji>outlook</kanji> for miles.
観.on: Far below, a pink <sound>car</sound>nation turns its head to face the lens.
観.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat climbs up beside the sparrow and stands on tiptoe to look too.

光.meaning: In a dark attic, you climb onto a wobbly <part>stool</part> and wipe the dusty window. A <part>sparkle</part> shoots through the gap and paints a gold stripe on the floor, with dust dancing in it. One thin beam: a <kanji>ray</kanji>.
光.on: The ray lands on a forgotten ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, which glows like a lamp.
光.kun: You hop down, land on one <sound>hee</sound>l, trip over a toy <sound>ca</sound>rp, and the beam lights up a painting of a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

歳.meaning: On the last night of the year, a guard puts up a <part>barricade</part> with a <part>stop</part> sign on top, and a <part>little</part> kid hides behind it to wait for midnight. Ten, nine, eight... the old calendar comes down. It's <kanji>year-end</kanji>.
歳.on: At midnight everyone toasts the new year with warm apple <sound>ci</sound>der.
歳.kun: A <sound>to</sound>tem pole gets one more notch carved in it, and a <sound>shee</sound>p bleats, one year older.

賃.meaning: There's no ticket machine on the little ferry. You <part>entrust</part> a <part>shellfish</part> to the boatman, he checks it's a good one and waves you aboard. One shell per trip, and no change given. That's the <kanji>fare</kanji>.
賃.on: The boatman bites the shell to test it, nods, and scratches his big <sound>chin</sound>.

影.meaning: At sunset, a cat sits on a hill in front of the <part>scenery</part>, and a long dark cat stretches across the grass behind it, with long <part>whiskers</part> made of shade. It copies every twitch. It's the cat's <kanji>shadow</kanji>.
影.on: A squirrel drops an <sound>a</sound>corn on the shadow's head, and the real cat looks up, puzzled.
影.kun: In the pond, a <sound>ca</sound>rp hides in the cat's shadow, and a <sound>ge</sound>cko darts across it.

徐.meaning: A <part>chairlift</part> loaded with far <part>too much</part> luggage creaks up the mountain one inch at a time. The skiers knit scarves while they wait. The top gets closer bit by bit: <kanji>gradually</kanji>.
徐.on: A <sound>jo</sound>gger running up the slope beside it waves as she overtakes.
徐.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>,' yawns a <sound>mo</sound>le in the next chair, as a <sound>moo</sound>se plods past them on foot.

緑.meaning: A gardener fills a <part>watering can</part> and pours it over a spool of white <part>thread</part>. Overnight the thread sprouts tiny leaves and moss, and by morning the whole spool is the shade of spring grass. It has turned <kanji>green</kanji>.
緑.on: She celebrates with a glass of <sound>Rio</sound>ja, while a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo sings from the mossy spool.
緑.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat, a <sound>do</sound>lphin and a fish from the <sound>ree</sound>f all queue up for a green scarf.

願.meaning: All the animals of the <part>meadow</part> want a pond, so a <part>rubber duck</part> waddles to the mayor's door with a scroll covered in hoofprints and pawprints. It bows and hands it over: please, dig us a pond. It's a <kanji>petition</kanji>.
願.on: The mayor reads it, then wipes a blob of muddy <sound>gun</sound>k off the bottom.
願.kun: The duck adds a gift, a <sound>ne</sound>t full of <sound>ga</sound>rlic, just to be sure.

涼.meaning: On the hottest day in the <part>capital</part>, the mayor switches on sprinklers on top of the tallest tower, and <part>water drops</part> mist down over the streets. Office workers stop and lift their faces. Ahh, that's <kanji>refreshing</kanji>.
涼.on: That night, everyone sleeps with the windows open at a little <sound>ryo</sound>kan inn.
涼.kun: A waiter brings cold <sound>su</sound>shi and a glass of yu<sound>zu</sound> juice on ice.

緒.meaning: <part>Someone</part> on the beach breaks a sandal, so they twist strong <part>thread</part> into a cord and loop it between their toes to hold the sole on. It works! Now it has a <kanji>thong</kanji>, the strap of a sandal.
緒.on: They hop to the beach <sound>sho</sound>p for a new pair, but it's closed.
緒.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' they sigh, as the cord snaps again.

寂.meaning: Under the <part>roof</part> of a huge empty house lives an old <part>uncle</part>. All the cousins have moved away, so he sets the table for one, chats to the clock and waves at the postman twice. Every room echoes. He's full of <kanji>loneliness</kanji>.
寂.on: So he buys a <sound>jacu</sound>zzi big enough for twenty and sits in it all alone, bubbling.
寂.kun: He shares his supper with a single <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a <sound>bee</sound> on the windowsill.

避.meaning: A thief races down the <part>ramp</part> into the market with the police close behind. At the last second he dives under a <part>chili stall</part>, and they run straight past, sneezing. He got away! He managed to <kanji>evade</kanji> them.
避.on: Then he slips on a chili and snaps the <sound>hee</sound>l off his shoe.
避.kun: He tiptoes off, ducking a <sound>sa</sound>rdine that flies from the fish stall.

海.meaning: <part>Every</part> one of the <part>water drops</part> that fall on the hills packs a tiny suitcase and sets off downhill: down the gutter, along a stream, over a waterfall. Splash! They all meet again in one huge, salty, wavy place. They've reached the <kanji>sea</kanji>.
海.on: On the beach, a boy flies a <sound>ki</sound>te shaped like a whale.
海.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasps a <sound>mee</sound>rkat, seeing the waves for the very first time.

舟.meaning: Look at the shape: a long frame with two dots inside, like two people sitting, and a bar across it for the oar. Two friends paddle it over a lake, splashing and arguing about whose turn it is to row. It's a little <kanji>boat</kanji>.
舟.on: When it springs a leak, they bail it out with a giant <sound>shoe</sound>.
舟.kun: They nap on a <sound>fu</sound>ton in the bottom and catch fish in a <sound>ne</sound>t.

航.meaning: A <part>boat</part> has lost its compass, so the captain sets a <part>cake stand</part> on deck with a candle on top and steers by the way the flame leans. Left at the lighthouse, right at the rocks, all the way home. That's how she can <kanji>navigate</kanji>.
航.on: To mark the route, she drops an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne overboard at every turn.

豚.meaning: Every full <part>moon</part>, the farmer's <part>pig</part> sneaks into the kitchen and reads the menu on the wall. Tonight it says 'roast with apple sauce', and its curly tail goes straight. It runs for the hills: it has no wish to be <kanji>pork</kanji>.
豚.on: The cook chases it round the yard, snapping a pair of kitchen <sound>ton</sound>gs.
豚.kun: The pig hides behind a <sound>bu</sound>lldozer, trembling under a giant <sound>ta</sound>co shell.

強.meaning: An <part>insect</part> no bigger than a grain of rice picks up a huge <part>bow</part>, braces its <part>elbow</part> and pulls the string back until the wood creaks. Twang! The arrow flies clean over the hill. Tiny, but very <kanji>strong</kanji>.
強.on: The arrow pins a newspaper to the wall of a street <sound>kio</sound>sk on the far side.
強.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' sneezes the insect, then lifts a whole pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt over its head.

張.meaning: An archer ties a <part>long</part> rope to the tip of his <part>bow</part> and pulls it across the yard, tighter and tighter, until it's as tight as a tightrope. Then he hangs out his washing on it. He knows how to <kanji>stretch</kanji> a line.
張.on: His pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker hangs on the line too, swinging in the wind.
張.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he laughs, as a cat strolls along the stretched rope.

頑.meaning: A <part>rubber duck</part> plants itself on a <part>sawhorse</part> in the middle of the road and won't budge. Cars honk, the mayor pleads, a bulldozer nudges it: nothing. It just stares straight ahead. What a <kanji>stubborn</kanji> duck.
頑.on: Someone has glued it down with a blob of green <sound>gun</sound>k, so it's stuck for good.
頑.kun: They try to bribe it with a <sound>ca</sound>rp, a <sound>ta</sound>co and a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock: it won't even blink.

多.meaning: One <part>evening</part> moon rises, then another right on top of it. More pop up behind those, until the sky is crowded with crescents bumping into each other. Two would be a lot, but tonight there are <kanji>many</kanji>.
多.on: The moons tumble into the bath and fill the whole <sound>tu</sound>b.
多.kun: '<sound>Ohh</sound>!' gasps everyone in the street, staring up at all those moons.

対.meaning: On one side of the lawn, a <part>dancer</part> spins and leaps; on the other, a golfer swings a <part>golf club</part>. They glare at each other: whose sport is better? The crowd picks sides and starts to chant. It's dance <kanji>versus</kanji> golf.
対.on: It ends in a draw, a <sound>tie</sound>, so they both get a medal.
対.kun: The dancer keeps one <sound>eye</sound> on the golfer, her <sound>te</sound>nnis opponent tomorrow.

相.meaning: A <part>tree</part> and an <part>eye</part> stare at each other across a field all day. The eye watches over the tree, and the tree watches over the eye; neither ever blinks. Each does the same for the other: it's <kanji>mutual</kanji>.
相.on: When it rains, they wash each other with the same bar of <sound>soa</sound>p.
相.kun: The eye winks at the tree, and the tree winks back with a knot shaped like an <sound>eye</sound>.

隣.meaning: Two houses share one wall. The house on the left flies a <part>pennant</part>; the one on the right keeps a sack of <part>rice</part> on the step. A man on <part>mismatched legs</part> hobbles back and forth between them, borrowing sugar. Side by side for ever, they're <kanji>neighboring</kanji>.
隣.on: He borrows a cup of sugar and gives back a gold <sound>rin</sound>g by mistake.
隣.kun: Next door has a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, an oven full of <sound>na</sound>an and a fish tank like a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

井.meaning: In the village square, <part>two</part> planks lie across a wooden <part>goal</part> frame, making a little grid like a # sign. Peer through the middle: far down, something glints and echoes. Drop a bucket in: it's a <kanji>well</kanji>.
井.on: Down at the bottom, the bucket clangs against an old iron <sound>sa</sound>fe.
井.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' shrieks a frog as the bucket lands on it.

丼.meaning: Look into the square frame of the <part>well</part>: one <part>dot</part> sits in the middle, like an egg yolk. Fill the frame with rice, lay slices of pork on top and crack an egg on top: dinner! It's a <kanji>bowl</kanji> of food.
丼.on: You lift the pork slices out of the pan with a pair of <sound>ton</sound>gs.
丼.kun: A <sound>don</sound>key, a <sound>bu</sound>ll and a fish from the <sound>ree</sound>f queue up for a bowl each.

港.meaning: At the end of the bay, the <part>water drops</part> go calm, and ships crowd in <part>together</part>, tied up side by side. A coil of rope lies on the dock like a <part>cobra</part> ready to strike. Sailors stroll ashore for dinner. The ships are safe in the <kanji>harbor</kanji>.
港.on: The first stall on the dock sells ice cream in a giant waffle <sound>co</sound>ne.
港.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat sells hot <sound>na</sound>an beside a <sound>to</sound>tem pole carved like a lighthouse.

寒.meaning: Under a freezing <part>roof</part>, the water in the <part>well</part> has frozen solid, and <part>one</part> extra plank is nailed over it. A man stands on top with his legs spread like an <part>eight</part>, and each icicle drips a frozen <part>dot</part> on the floor. Brrr! It's bitterly <kanji>cold</kanji>.
寒.on: To cheer up the room, he puts a frozen pink <sound>car</sound>nation in a jar.
寒.kun: A <sound>sa</sound>rdine freezes in the bucket, and a <sound>moo</sound>se knocks at the door asking for a blanket.

傘.meaning: In a downpour, two pairs of <part>twins</part> squeeze under one open <part>umbrella</part>, all four gripping the <part>ten</part>-shaped cross of its handle. Feet stick out, elbows bump, and someone always gets a wet ear. One <kanji>umbrella</kanji>, four kids.
傘.on: When the rain stops, they share an ice cream <sound>sun</sound>dae underneath it anyway.
傘.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp and a <sound>sa</sound>rdine swim up the flooded street and shelter under it too.

腐.meaning: In the cellar of the <part>government office</part>, someone has left a parcel of <part>meat</part> waiting for the right form to be stamped. Three months later it's still waiting, green and fuzzy, and the whole building stinks. The paperwork made it <kanji>rot</kanji>.
腐.on: The clerk who sleeps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton by the filing cabinets finally wakes up and gags.
腐.kun: A <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the clock to complain, and even the cat won't touch the <sound>sa</sound>rdine beside it.

銭.meaning: A tiny blacksmith melts a lump of <part>gold</part>, pours it into little round cups and hangs the discs to cool on a <part>spear rack</part>, one on each prong. Clink, clink! Each disc gets a face stamped on it. Now it's a <kanji>coin</kanji>.
銭.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try guards the rack all night with a spear of his own.
銭.kun: He bites a coin to test it, tastes lemon <sound>ze</sound>st, and drops it on his k<sound>nee</sound>.
